newsitem.title: USA: Tampa-Hillsborough Cty, Fla, expressway plans debt.
newsitem.headline: Tampa-Hillsborough Cty, Fla, expressway plans debt.

text.p: Florida's Tampa-Hillsborough County Expressway Authority is seeking authorization to issue up to $300 million of revenue bonds, including a $137 million refunding that will convert its outstanding general obligation debt to revenue bonds.
The proposal will go before state Cabinet officials for authorization on Sept 26, and then to the state Supreme Court for validation.
"We'll probably be looking at the first issue, if everything goes smoothly, some time in February or March," said authority spokesman Harold Aldrich.
The first issue of about $137 million will include $125 million to refund GO bonds issued in 1971 and 1978, and $12 million to finance several small road projects.
The authority's outstanding bonds are not traditional GOs. They are backed by toll revenues and by receipts from a county gas tax, which are held in a state trust fund.

"If there's a shortfall in toll revenues, they reach in there and tap that gas tax fund. There getting the state's GO with the state pledging gas tax dollars that belong to the county anyway. The state is really not on the hook to pay anything," said the authority's financial adivser, Charles LeCroy at Raymond James & Associates Inc.
The new revenue bonds will be AAA-insured, so borrowing costs will probably be equal to those backed by the state's AA-rated GO pledge, LeCroy said.
The main reason or the refunding is to revise the bond documents to improve the authority's flexibility, LeCroy and Aldrich said.
"We're operating under bond documents that are 30 years old. They're very antiquated." said Aldrich.
The old documents do not allow for public-private partnership projects. They also require that any excess toll revenues be used to retire outstanding debt, rather than to fund new projects.
The GO bonds require 133 percent coverage, while the revenue bonds would require only about 125 percent, even though the authority will seek to show it has 150 percent, LeCroy said.
The bonds will be sold by competitive bid through the Florida Division of Bond Finance.

The authority will probably do a second bond issue 18 to 24 months after the first to finance new projects, but will not necessarily use all of the remaining $163 million from the $300 million authorization.
